name: Electrical Storm and Incessant Ventricular Tachycardia

clinicalPearls: Electrical storm (VT/VF storm) is defined as three or more episodes of ventricular tachycardia or ventricular fibrillation within 24 hours, each requiring intervention to terminate (Harrison 22e p.1972).

It is uncommon in the general population but carries great concern because, untreated, it follows a rapid course that can lead to death; prompt recognition and intervention are essential (Harrison 22e p.1972).
Storm occurs in about 4% of patients with a primary-prevention ICD but in as many as 20% of patients with prior known VT or resuscitated sudden death (Harrison 22e p.1972).
VT is termed incessant when it recurs shortly after electrical, pharmacologic, or spontaneous conversion to sinus rhythm; it is typically monomorphic (Harrison 22e p.1972).
A slow incessant monomorphic VT may rarely escape ICD detection because its rate falls below the programmed detection threshold (Harrison 22e p.1972).
Antiarrhythmic drugs themselves can be proarrhythmic and render VT incessant (e.g., amiodarone or a sodium-channel blocker such as flecainide) (Harrison 22e p.1972).

Multiple ICD shocks constitute a medical emergency warranting activation of emergency medical services; patients should never drive themselves to hospital after receiving a shock (Harrison 22e p.1972).
After any ICD shock, device interrogation is crucial to confirm therapy was delivered for a true ventricular arrhythmia rather than for lead malfunction or an atrial arrhythmia (Harrison 22e p.1972).
Antitachycardia pacing terminates over 70% of VT episodes-even rapid VT-so appropriate ICD programming markedly reduces shocks and improves quality of life (Harrison 22e p.1972).
Programming VF detection zones above 220 beats/min in primary-prevention ICDs and using longer detection times significantly reduce unnecessary and inappropriate shocks (Harrison 22e p.1972).

Determining whether the storming rhythm is monomorphic or polymorphic guides management, as does inspecting initiation/termination patterns on stored ICD electrograms for precipitating factors (Harrison 22e p.1973).
Reducing sympathetic drive is a core management principle: stellate ganglion block and upper thoracic epidural anesthesia can restore stability in some patients (Harrison 22e p.1973).
harrison.pathophysiology: Electrical storm reflects repeated, often rapidly recurring ventricular tachyarrhythmias arising from an unstable myocardial substrate combined with heightened sympathetic drive and acute triggering factors. Substrates vary: in the setting of acute myocardial ischemia/infarction, surviving Purkinje cells within infarcted myocardium can show triggered automaticity, generating recurrent polymorphic VT/VF. PVC-initiated polymorphic VT/VF can also occur without infarction or ischemia (idiopathic VF), where triggering premature ventricular contractions arise from fascicular tissue or papillary muscles, sometimes from scarred myocardium seen on cardiac MRI. Other substrates include acquired or congenital long QT (torsades des pointes from abnormal repolarization), Brugada syndrome (right ventricular outflow tract/epicardial substrate), and inflammatory cardiomyopathies. Incessant VT is usually monomorphic and may be driven or sustained by the proarrhythmic action of antiarrhythmic drugs (Harrison 22e p.1972-1974).
additionalDifferentials: Acute coronary syndrome / myocardial ischemia precipitating polymorphic VT or VF
Acquired or congenital long QT syndrome with torsades des pointes
Inflammatory cardiomyopathy (giant cell myocarditis, cardiac sarcoidosis, viral myocarditis)
Idiopathic PVC-initiated polymorphic VT/VF from fascicular tissue or papillary muscles
infectionMimics: Viral myocarditis presenting with VT/VF storm
nonInfectiousMimics: Lead malfunction or atrial arrhythmia causing inappropriate ICD shocks rather than true ventricular arrhythmia
additionalInvestigations: ICD interrogation to confirm appropriate ventricular detection/therapy and to review stored electrograms for arrhythmia onset and triggers
ECG monitoring to classify the rhythm as monomorphic versus polymorphic and to assess the QT interval and Brugada pattern (Rsr' with ST elevation in V1/V2)
Serum electrolyte assessment, especially potassium and magnesium
Evaluation for ischemia / acute coronary syndrome and cardiac function
Cardiac MRI to detect scarred myocardium when PVC-initiated polymorphic VT/VF is suspected
Endomyocardial biopsy when a new inflammatory cardiomyopathy is suspected in a patient without prior cardiac disease
redFlags: Polymorphic VT or VF, especially if accompanied by features of acute coronary syndrome
Hemodynamically unstable or recurrent ventricular arrhythmia requiring repeated cardioversion
Signs of gradual cardiac decompensation in a hemodynamically stable but incessant VT
New-onset frequent ventricular arrhythmia in a patient with no known prior cardiac disease (consider inflammatory myocarditis)
harrison.prognosis: Spontaneous ventricular arrhythmias-particularly those requiring shock for termination-are associated with an increased subsequent risk of death and hospitalization in patients with depressed ventricular function. Untreated storm progresses rapidly and can be fatal, but catheter ablation, antiarrhythmic drug therapy, and adjunctive measures can be life-saving. An arrhythmic episode should prompt reevaluation for declining cardiac function, ischemia, or intercurrent illness (Harrison 22e p.1972).
pitfalls: Assuming every ICD shock reflects a true ventricular arrhythmia-lead malfunction or an atrial arrhythmia can trigger inappropriate shocks, so interrogation is required (Harrison 22e p.1972).

Overlooking that interventions to control the arrhythmia may themselves worsen outcome-most antiarrhythmics can cause bradycardia requiring ICD pacing, which can itself impair ventricular function (Harrison 22e p.1972).
Failing to recognize antiarrhythmic proarrhythmia as a cause of incessant VT (Harrison 22e p.1972).
Missing a slow incessant monomorphic VT that falls outside programmed ICD detection parameters (Harrison 22e p.1972).
Not searching for a treatable substrate (ischemia, long QT, Brugada, inflammatory cardiomyopathy) that dictates specific therapy (Harrison 22e p.1974).
harrison.severityClassification: Defined event: electrical storm = >=3 episodes of VT or VF within 24 h each requiring intervention to terminate. VT is classified as monomorphic versus polymorphic, and as sustained versus incessant; substrate-based categories include ischemic, long QT, Brugada, PVC-initiated, and inflammatory (Harrison 22e p.1972-1974).
